Laura — thanks for the call this morning. Priya and I pulled together the traffic sample + a couple notes on our SLA constraints. Attaching a short CSV with 10k anonymized request events; fields: timestamp, request_type, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms. High level context: expected steady-state 120 reqs/s during business hours, with 10x burst for a few minutes during syncs. 99th p90 latency requirement is <= 250ms for user-facing flows.

Two quick asks for the MAP: can Redwood run the unit-cost simulation with both (A) no prefix caching and (B) a 35% prefix hit rate to show delta across tokens/$? Also curious on the batching assumptions you'd use if we set a per-request latency SLO at 200ms.

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit cost simulation ask

Samir — received, thanks. Quick notes and proposed next steps below.

Summary of what we'll deliver as part of the MAP econ check:
- Run deterministic sim across your provided sample for three scenarios: (1) no prefix cache, (2) 35% prefix cache, (3) 60% warm-cache (to show optimistic upside).
- Report tokens per user/session, per-token $ breakdown, and simulated QPS cost at 3 latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
- Provide a short ops checklist for enabling prefix cache and a recommended batching window tuned to keep p99 <= 200ms where possible.

Clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Are completion lengths capped at 256 tokens in production? Your sample shows a long tail up to ~1,200 tokens.
2) What's the acceptable cost uplift for ops-led features (we often provide trade-off curves; we can show cost vs p99 vs cache hit).

Proposed timeline (MAP milestones):
- 6/21: Redwood runs initial sim and posts results + assumptions doc (we'll attach redwood-sim-parameters.xlsx).
- 6/22: 30-min readout with your engineering and product team to agree acceptance gates.
- 6/25: If gates pass, we'll prepare a canary plan (1-week run) and a Dedicated capacity cost estimate for steady-state.

I've attached our sim parameter workbook and will run the first pass this afternoon. Looping in Karthik and Ben on ops/fin gates.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mednovus.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit cost simulation ask

Laura — quick answers inline: 
> 1) Are completion lengths capped at 256 tokens in production?
We currently enforce a soft cap of 512 tokens for conversational assistants; some back-end batch processors spawn longer completions (up to 1,200) for transcripts. For the user-facing flows (the 120 reqs/s), assume 256 tokens cap.

> 2) What's the acceptable cost uplift for ops-led features?
We can tolerate up to a 35% increase on current infra spend for a measurable quality improvement. Above that we'll need to pair with visible SLA gains or business KPIs.

Also, the 35% prefix hit is our conservative engineering expectation after enabling warm-prefix population. We can push for 50% in optimized flows but want to see the middle-case first.

I'll be on the 6/22 readout. Attaching a sample warmup script snippet and a short latency histogram from last week's pilot.

—Samir

Attachment: mednovus-warmup-snippet.txt (text/plain, 3KB)
Attachment: latency-hist-weekly.png (image/png, 120KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: MAP gating acceptance checklist (draft)

Internal note — draft acceptance gates to propose at the readout with MedNovus: 

Gating acceptance (MAP econ + ops):
- Baseline tokens/$: sim must show < $0.015 per convo (median conv length assumed 80 tokens total) for the no-cache scenario to proceed to canary.
- Cache delta: 35% prefix hit must reduce tokens/$ by >= 12% relative to no-cache in the simulation.
- Latency: In canary, steer for p95 <= 180ms and p99 <= 250ms for user-facing traffic; if simulated p99 > 320ms, fail gate.
- Batching policy: recommend dynamic batching with max window 12ms for user flows; include a fallback to single-request path for high-priority traces.
- Simulation artifacts: sim report + raw run CSVs (tokens-per-request, batch sizes, simulated throughput) must be uploaded to the HubSpot deal record and Drive link.
- Financial ask: include estimated monthly committed cost for Dedicated at steady-state QPS and an incremental monthly add-on for a 10% capacity buffer.

Action items for readout: 
1) Confirm MedNovus accepts our three-scenario sim output and the acceptance gates above.
2) Agree on canary dates (target start 6/28) and success monitoring (cost burn + latency + cache hit).
3) If accepted, Ben to prepare Dedicated cost estimate for 6/25 signoff.

I'll tidy this into a one-pager before the readout.

—Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
